problem:
Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P19.1, P19.2, P19.3, P19.4. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
11     Residual hybrid entropy and YTD questions
Active items: P19.1, P19.2, P19.3, P19.4. Status: Open in the residual scope.

11.1    Atomic targets
P19.1 (T5): Entropy slopes of arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays
Prove the remaining entropy-slope statement for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays on a com-
pact Kähler manifold, outside the stated smooth polarized projective maximal-ray results.
State the non-Archimedean datum, the entropy normalization and the precise ray hypothe-
ses.

P19.2 (T4): Approximation preserving energy, entropy and singularities
Construct model approximations in the residual hybrid programme that preserve all required
energy, entropy and singularity data. Convergence of energy alone is insuﬃcient, and the
published/source-stated projective Fujita regimes are established subcases.

P19.3 (T5): Hybrid compactness and measures for degenerating families
Prove the compactness and measure-continuity statements needed along genuinely degener-
ating families of compact Kähler manifolds. A ﬁxed quasi-projective variety hybridized with
explicit scale factors is a diﬀerent known endpoint.

P19.4 (T5): Equivariant, transcendental and singular hybrid extensions
Establish the required automorphism-equivariant transcendental and singular extensions, with
the exact stability and metric signatures speciﬁed. Retain the residual distinctions from the
cited smooth polarized projective and static Kähler-class correspondences.

11.2    What constitutes a solution
Freeze the exact ray, approximation, family or equivariant signature and prove the residual
statement with its entropy and energy normalizations. Keep recent preprint claims in their
stated smooth polarized scope. The four targets are independent residual hybrid goals; they
are not prerequisites for the already cited static uniform-model-stability-to-cscK implication.

11.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
Problem 11.1. Develop the remaining entropy-slope, approximation, compactness, and au-
tomorphism statements for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays and degenerating families in the
hybrid K-stability/YTD programme on a compact Kähler manifold.

    The static projective entropy and stability gap must not be listed as wholly open at this
cutoﬀ. Boucksom–Jonsson’s version-two notes of 19 May 2026 give a structural complex-to-
non-Archimedean overview and only sketch a version of the cscK YTD argument [BJ26]. They
are used here as orientation, not as a separate approximation or hybrid-continuity theorem
that narrows any atom in Problem 11.1.
    Trusiani’s version-two preprint of 17 August 2026, [Tru26, Theorem B and Corollary A],
retains the special Fujita approximations for big line bundles and the claimed solution
of the Boucksom–Jonsson entropy-regularization conjecture; its Theorem A retains the
automorphism-relative uniform YTD theorem for smooth polarized projective varieties.
Corollary A also records the resulting equality of the Archimedean entropy slope along a

                                              76

maximal ﬁnite-energy ray with the non-Archimedean entropy, in that projective framework.
The new Appendix by Sébastien Boucksom supplies a non-Archimedean proof over k((t)),
and Theorem C adds the weighted-relative correspondence, including Calabi extremal met-
rics when the weight is log-concave. These are recent preprint claims, rather than results
independently reproved in this book. Boucksom–Jonsson’s 18 September 2025 preprint
[BJ25c] gives a non-Archimedean formulation for cscK and weighted extremal metrics on
polarized projective manifolds. Darvas–Zhang’s 3 November 2025 version-two preprint [DZ25,
Theorems 1.6 and 5.5] gives a uniform YTD correspondence for a unique cscK metric on an
arbitrary compact Kähler manifold using K β -stability and, in the polarized projective case, a
reductivity-plus-log-discrepancy-model formulation. Mesquita–Piccione–Witt Nyström prove
that uniform model stability implies existence in a Kähler class and establish the transcen-
dental ﬁnite-energy Calabi–Yau homeomorphism [MPWN25, Theorems A and B]. Finally,
Trusiani’s Corollary B identiﬁes the standard automorphism-relative projective stability
formulations in the smooth polarized setting [Tru26]. Thus the projective entropy slope, the
weighted-relative correspondence in the stated smooth polarized scope, and comparison of
the listed projective signatures are no longer open problems.
    There is a complementary hybrid endpoint outside the compact proper setting. For each
of the three aﬃne/Calabi-model situations stated in Wang’s Theorem B, explicit scale fac-
tors make the Archimedean potential and its non-Archimedean counterpart into one continu-
ous function on the hybrid space; the correspondingly rescaled Archimedean Monge–Ampère
measures converge weakly to the non-Archimedean measure [Wan25, Theorem B]. This is a
comparison for a ﬁxed quasi-projective variety over the hybrid parameter, not a compactness
or measure-continuity theorem for a degenerating family of compact Kähler manifolds. It
therefore does not discharge P19.3.
    Consequently, the atoms in Problem 11.1 are not asserted to be logical prerequisites for the
cited uniform-model-stability-to-cscK implication. They record the distinct residual hybrid
programme: statements for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays, log-discrepancy-model regu-
larization, and genuinely degenerating families that are not supplied merely by the static
Kähler-class theorem.
    Book Chapter 66, Book Chapter 68 separates hybrid convergence from entropy and coerciv-
ity. The BHJ erratum is enforced in Book Chapter 65. The remaining targets are narrower:
direct algebraic proofs of the known projective equivalences; K β -stability in the presence
of nontrivial automorphisms; equivariant transcendental and singular extensions; regulariza-
tion of rays attached to log-discrepancy models; and the genuinely hybrid compactness and
measure-continuity statements needed to pass through a degenerating family. Boucksom–
Jonsson also isolate bounded support size for divisorial test measures, algebraic equivariance
proofs, and extension to polarized klt pairs [BJ25c, Questions and further remarks]. Those
residual problems remain open; the smooth polarized projective entropy and weighted-relative
theorems are dated Trusiani version-two claims, not missing inputs.
